headlines.title: 1 injured after shooting on Bay Bridge
headlines.description: A person was hurt following a shooting on the Bay Bridge Saturday morning, the California Highway Patrol said. CHP said the shooting was reported around 4:06 a.m. on eastbound I-80, east of Treasure Island, on the San Francisco-Oakland Bay Bridge. Authorities said the victim reported he had sustained a gunshot wound in the leg and was self-transporting to a local hospital for treatment. CHP said all eastbound lanes of I-80 on the Bay Bridge were closed for approximately an hour due to the investigation. An additional search was conducted just after 2 p.m., which closed eastbound lanes for around 30 minutes, CHP added. Authorities said they are working to identify the suspects in the incident and asked anyone with information to contact the CHP tip line at 707-917-4491.

headlines.title: Missing Oakland woman was looking at trails before disappearing, investigator says
headlines.description: A new clue has emerged in the case of a missing East Bay woman. Amy Hillyard, co-owner of Farley’s coffee shops, has been missing for more than six months. Hillyard was last seen walking near her Oakland home on March 25. She left without her phone or wallet. But now, Hillyard’s friends and family have a new sense of hope after learning a new clue in the case has emerged. Private investigator Steve Fischer, who was hired by Hillyard’s family, says a deep forensics dive of her home computer has revealed she spent 33 minutes looking at eight different trails in Oakland and Berkeley the morning before she disappeared. He says five of those trails have not been on their radar and haven’t been searched yet. “This is the biggest break in the case since I’ve been on board. I told the family there’s no guarantees here, but we are going on something that feels like we’re not searching blindly. We actually have a reason for being in these areas,” Fischer said. On Saturday, a group of volunteers, including Monica, are gearing up to start searching for those trails tomorrow. All of them hope the new clue leads to Hillyard.

headlines.title: Man dead after shooting at Dublin Sports Grounds
headlines.description: A man died following a shooting at the Dublin Sports Grounds on Saturday, Dublin Police Services said. Dublin Police Services said officers responded to a shooting around 3:08 p.m. at 6700 Dublin Blvd. Authorities said a man was found on the parking lot with multiple gunshot wounds, and he was pronounced dead at the scene. Officials said all known suspects are in custody but did not specify the number of suspects involved.

headlines.title: Valkyries excitement continues ahead of WNBA playoffs
headlines.description: The Golden State Valkyries are making another historic run into the playoffs, and the Bay Area is getting ready for “Ballhalla” on Sunday night. Chase Center, Thrive City and sports bars across the Bay Area will be covered in violet and rocking as they cheer on this second-year expansion team while it continues its unbelievable rise in the ranks of the WNBA. Thom Jensen has the full report in the video above.

headlines.title: Supply chain inflation: How rising diesel prices will impact consumers
headlines.description: Get ready for the domino effect from rising fuel prices. Diesel prices are now hovering at record levels and experts warn of “supply chain inflation” where the increased costs will be passed on to customers. NBC Bay Area’s Damian Trujillo has more in the video above. Bay Area Sep 25 Oil & Gas Sep 24 oil and gas Sep 22 California gas and diesel prices surge to record highs, hammering farmers and drivers

headlines.title: Good Neighbor Week kicks off in San Francisco
headlines.description: On Saturday, the community gathered at San Francisco’s Civic Center to recognize Good Neighbor Award winners and start a week that aims to bring connection and kindness to neighbors. At Civic Center, the welcome mat was laid out as San Francisco Good Neighbor Week kicked off. Julia Gitis is the event’s founder and organizer, and explained that she first learned about something called “Good Neighbor Day.” “That was started by President Jimmy Carter in the 70s. It’s not widely known, but we brought it to San Francisco last year for the first time. We are the first city in California to celebrate it, we’re celebrating it with a whole week,” Gitis said. The event included music, a lively atmosphere and neighborhood representation from all city districts. This day also included recognition for Good Neighbor Award winners. One of those people was A-Jay Nicolas, who is a founding member that’s getting a neighborhood association up and running. “We’ve already started participating in conversations around the neighborhood, trying to get people’s pulse on what they want to see in Mission Bay what they want to fix, what they think is going well,” he said. There are community partners, an events calendar for people to know what exists and custom events for the week, but the key is connection. Nearby a trash cleanup was underway. One participant says it happens regularly with “Refuse Refuse”, a way to help and they also meet people.

headlines.title: Warriors sign star Steph Curry to reported two-year, $116M contract extension
headlines.description: The Warriors might not have made many moves this offseason, but they made the most important one on Friday evening. Golden State signed superstar point guard Steph Curry agreed to a contract extension, the team announced. The new deal is for two years, $116 million and includes a player option for the 2028-29 NBA season, ESPN’s Shams Charania reported Friday, citing sources. Curry became eligible for an extension of up to two years and $136.7 million on Aug. 29 coming off his current one-year, $62.6 million expiring deal. But he took $20 million less to continue his career in the Bay. After the Warriors missed the playoffs following an up-and-down 2025-26 season, there was speculation, as there always is, that Curry could look elsewhere and be more competitive as he reaches the tail end of his career. But the speculation was just that, as the two-time NBA MVP will continue in Year 18 with the only NBA team he’s known. And, like the rest of the team, he could return with a vengeance. Curry missed nearly 30 games over two months dealing with runner’s knee. His co-star, Jimmy Butler, also dealt with his own injury, although it was a season-ending ACL injury in January. There is strong belief within the organization that had Curry and Butler not been injured, the Warriors’ 2025-26 season would have ended much differently. But the past is the past. Curry and his Dubs now are focused on the present and getting back to the top of the West. Last season, Curry averaged 26.6 points on 46.8-percent shooting from the field and 39.3 percent from 3-point range, with 3.6 rebounds, 4.7 assists and 1.1 steals in 34 minutes through 43 games. headlines.title: Police investigate burglary and shooting in San Francisco
headlines.description: San Francisco police said they are investigating a burglary and a shooting that were reported at different times on Saturday morning. Police said officers responded to the 1200 block of 22nd Ave. around 5:08 a.m. regarding a burglary that had just occurred. At the scene, officers met with the victim, who authorities say fired a gun during the incident. The suspect left the scene and was not found by officers, according to the police department. Minutes later, around 5:28 a.m., police said officers responded to the 400 block of 47th Ave. regarding a shooting. At the scene, responding officers located a person suffering from an apparent gunshot wound, authorities said. The victim was taken to the hospital with non-life-threatening injuries, according to the police department. Police said this is an active investigation and clarified they have not confirmed whether the person who was shot is connected to the burglary.

headlines.title: Fans prepare to say goodbye to Bay Area legend Mike Krukow
headlines.description: Giants fans are preparing to say goodbye to Bay Area legend Mike Krukow. Krukow will call his final game on Sunday, ending a 36-year run in the broadcast booth. For generations of fans, Mike Krukow and Duane Kuiper have been part of the family, calling games together since 1990. On Sunday, fans are getting one last chance to hear “Kruk and Kuip” together in the booth. The Giants and Dodgers opened their three-game series on Thursday at Oracle Park, with Krukow’s final series marking the end of an era. Krukow announced his retirement in August. The 74-year-old has said he doesn’t really want to, but needs to, as he battles a degenerative muscle disease. It’s a decision that wasn’t easy to share with fans or with his broadcast partner, who’s been by his side for more than three decades. “It was the hardest thing I had to do was walk away from him. We’ve been through so much life together, I didn’t know if there was a perfect time or a perfect place then in the end in the lunchroom. I said I think I’m done and he says ‘No, you’re not’,” Krukow told NBC Bay Area’s Raj Mathai. It’s a friendship that started when they were Giants teammates but grew into so much more. “Kruk and Kuip” became the soundtrack for all Giants fans, which included three World Series titles. San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie declared Thursday as “Kruk and Kuip Day” in the city. As Krukow gets ready for his final game, there’s one thing he wants his fans to know. “I’m going to tell them just how much they mean to me and my family on the last day. I don’t know if you can convey it in words, but it’ll be conveyed in emotion. That I can guarantee,” he said. The Giants will honor Krukow after Sunday’s season finale at Oracle Park, with fans getting a chance to celebrate his career and that incredible partnership with “Kuip.” For many, it’ll be a celebration, but also an emotional goodbye.

headlines.title: Hillsborough police investigate crash involving juvenile riding an e-bike
headlines.description: Hillsborough police said they are investigating a collision involving an e-bike that occurred on Friday. Police say the collision was reported just before 3:50 p.m. in the area of Macadamia Drive, and it reportedly involved a vehicle and a bicyclist. At the scene, police said responding officers determined the incident was a solo-collision involving a juvenile riding an electric bike, and no other vehicles were involved.

headlines.title: Electrical problem causes Vallejo police officer's SUV to catch fire
headlines.description: A Vallejo police officer’s SUV caught fire on Thursday in Fairfield, according to authorities. The incident occurred on I-80, near the Abernathy Road exit in Fairfield. As soon as the officer saw smoke coming from the rear of the cruiser, the officer pulled over right away and got out safely. Fire crews arrived quickly to put out the flames, which intensified after road flares, stored inside the SUV ignited. Investigators say an electrical problem in the rear of the vehicle caused that fire.

headlines.title: Vallejo conservationist says she was unjustly arrested while volunteering
headlines.description: A well-known North Bay conservationist says she was unjustly arrested and manhandled on Wednesday while doing the volunteer duties she’s been doing for years. Myrna Hayes, 70, of Vallejo, was arrested at Mare Island’s San Pablo Bay Trail on Wednesday during her nightly routine of locking the gates to the trail. “I’ve been locking this gate. I go 3/4 of a mile on the gravel road every night, going on 17 years,” Hayes said. Vallejo police say they had received a call from a City of Vallejo Public Works employee reporting suspicious activity at the preserve that night. They say the employee who called was assigned to perform standard evening checks, including securing the perimeter gates after closing hours and inspecting the grounds for signs of vandalism of theft. That’s when police say he saw a vehicle containing a driver and a passenger that “were unauthorized to be on the premises.” Police say the employee gave the VPD Communications Division “detailed descriptions of both the individuals and their vehicle.” Police say responding officers found a vehicle matching the description in the area. Before attempting a traffic stop, authorities say the vehicle pulled over abruptly, and the driver “immediately exited the car to approach the police vehicle.” Hayes says she initially didn’t realize they were police and was trying to clear the park before locking it. Police say they tried to detain the driver, who “refused to comply with basic commands”. They said the driver remained non-compliant despite continuous requests from officers to control her movements, which led to her arrest. “That’s when he physically grabbed me and handcuffed me,” Hayes said. “I know that he took me another time and smashed me against his car.” Hayes says the encounter left her with a bruised eye, swollen legs and body pains. Three patrols cars and six officers responded to the scene. Hayes was taken to jail, where she spent 12 hours before being released Thursday morning. Hayes says she’s baffled and angry. “I’ve never been in jail. I’ve never been touched by a police officer. I’ve never been charged with anything other than a speeding ticket in college,” she said. Civil Rights Attorney Melissa Nold believes the police response is bizarre, adding a 70-year-old unarmed woman didn’t warrant this kind of escalation. “Everyone knows Myrna, everybody loves Myrna. She’s a kind soul,” Nold said. “You’re supposed to take the path of least resistance, not go turbo charge when you’re dealing with a 70-year-old woman who’s been out here serving our community for decades.” Hayes has been serving as the unpaid caretaker and tour guide for Mare Island shoreline for three decades and was even featured on NBC Bay Area’s “Bay Area Proud” for being a steward of the wetlands. She says the encounter with the police has left her shaken. Vallejo police said, “Follow-up investigation verified that neither the driver nor the passenger were city employees, and had no legal authority or operational responsibility at the preserve after hours.”
